2027-04-10.title: Second Saturday of Resurrection
2027-04-10.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts
2027-04-10.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). The Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost.
2027-04-10.verse: Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself. Touch me and see; for a ghost does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have.
theo: Paul's letter to the Colossians describes the new life of those who have been raised with Christ in Baptism. Just before today's passage he tells them to put on, like new clothes, “compassion, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience,” and to forgive one another as the Lord has forgiven them. Then comes the garment that holds all the others together: “Above all, clothe yourselves with love, which binds everything together in perfect harmony.” Love is the belt that keeps the other virtues from falling off. Then Paul gives three gifts for a Christian home and community. The first: “let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, to which indeed you were called in the one body. And be thankful.” The word ‘rule’ is the word for an umpire in the games: when we are pulled in different directions, the peace of Christ is to make the call. The second: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly.” Not visit occasionally, but dwell, live in the house, have its own room. The third: “with gratitude in your hearts sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs to God.” A Christian family that prays together, reads the Gospel together and sings together is a small church. Kerala Christian homes have long kept this at dusk, when the lamp is lit and the family gathers for evening prayer: that moment is Colossians 3 lived out. Saturday is also the day the Church honours the Blessed Virgin Mary, who kept all the words of her Son and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19): she is the model of the word of Christ dwelling richly in a home.

Paul ends with a rule that covers all of life: “And whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.” There is nothing too ordinary to be done in the name of Jesus: cooking, studying, driving, nursing, ploughing. And everything is to be done with thanksgiving. The Greek word for giving thanks is the root of the word Eucharist; the Syriac word Qurbana means the offering. A Christian life is meant to become one long Qurbana: an offering of everything to the Father, through the Son, with thanks.

In the Gospel we are back on Easter evening in Jerusalem. The two disciples from Emmaus are telling their story when “Jesus himself stood among them and said to them, ‘Peace be with you.’” The disciples were terrified: “They were startled and terrified, and thought that they were seeing a ghost.” Jesus answers with a tenderness that is almost humorous: “Why are you frightened, and why do doubts arise in your hearts? Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself. Touch me and see; for a ghost does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have.” Then, because they are still disbelieving for joy, he asks, “Have you anything here to eat?” “They gave him a piece of broiled fish, and he took it and ate in their presence.” Luke insists on the body because the faith of the Church depends on it. The Resurrection is not a beautiful idea, a memory, or a vision; the One who was crucified is alive in his own body, glorified and no longer subject to death, yet the same body that bears the wounds. That is why Christians bury their dead with reverence and wait for the resurrection of the body. And the One who ate fish with his friends gives himself to us as food at every Holy Qurbana: his true Body and Blood, risen and living.
conn: “As many of you as were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ” (Galatians 3:27).
“Many waters cannot quench love, neither can floods drown it” (Song of Songs 8:7); “the greatest of these is love” (1 Corinthians 13:13).
The priestly blessing: “the LORD lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace” (Numbers 6:26); Jesus' first word on Easter evening is “Peace be with you” (Luke 24:36).
“O sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth” (Psalm 96:1); “be filled with the Spirit… singing and making melody to the Lord in your hearts” (Ephesians 5:18–19).
In my flesh I shall see God.
Job's hope: “then in my flesh I shall see God” (Job 19:26).
Peter tells Cornelius that the apostles are witnesses “who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead” (Acts 10:41); John: “what we have looked at and touched with our hands” (1 John 1:1).
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Risen Lord stands among us and says, Peace be with you. He gives us not a memory but himself, his glorified Body and Blood, truly present.
The whole Qurbana is thanksgiving: everything we have done in word and deed during the week is brought to the altar and offered to the Father through the Son.
outline: The lamp lit at dusk and the family gathered to pray.
The belt that holds the virtues together.
Point 2 · The peace of Christ rule

The home as a little church.

live: Gather the family for prayer every evening this week, light the lamp, read a few lines of the Gospel and sing one hymn.
Before an important decision this week, ask: what keeps the peace of Christ in my heart?
Begin your work each morning with the sign of the cross and a short thanksgiving.
Visit the grave of a family member and pray for them, in hope of the resurrection of the body.
fathers: I know and believe that he was in the flesh even after the Resurrection. When he came to Peter and those with him, he said, Take hold of me, touch me and see that I am not a spirit without a body. They touched him at once and believed. After his Resurrection he ate and drank with them as one who has flesh, though he was spiritually one with the Father.
Singing belongs to the one who loves. The new song is sung by the new man, who has been made new by love; let your life sing, so that your voice does not sing alone.
magis: The Risen Jesus establishes direct contact with his disciples through touch and the sharing of a meal; his body is the same body that was crucified, bearing the marks of his Passion, yet now with new properties of a glorious body.
Christ is raised with his own body: ‘See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself’; so in him all will rise again with their own bodies.
The Eucharist is a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the Father, a blessing by which the Church expresses her gratitude to God for all his benefits.
Song and music are woven into the liturgy; they express prayer more beautifully, unite the assembly and give greater solemnity to the rites.
The Christian family is a communion of persons and can and should be called a domestic church, a community of faith, hope and charity.
saints: Monday 5 to Saturday 10 April: the second week of the Resurrection. Sunday 11 April: the Third Sunday of Resurrection. The Latin Church keeps the Annunciation of the Lord on Monday 5 April this year (moved from 25 March, which fell on Pesaha Thursday); Syro-Malabar faithful follow the direction of their eparchy.
2027-04-10.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you stood among your frightened disciples and said, Peace be with you; you showed them your hands and your feet and ate before them. Strengthen our faith in your true Resurrection and in the resurrection of the body. Clothe us with love above all, let your peace rule in our hearts, and let your word dwell in our homes richly, so that with grateful hearts we may sing to the Father and do everything in your name. With the Blessed Virgin Mary, who kept your words in her heart, we praise you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

2027-04-10.question: Does the word of Christ live in my home, or only visit on Sundays?
catechism: The real body of the Risen Lord.
kidsaint: St Chavara Achan was a priest in Kerala who loved families. He told parents to pray together every day with their children, and he wrote a letter of advice for families that is still read today. He also started schools so that every child could learn. Lesson: a family that prays together is a little church where Jesus lives!
2027-04-10.special: Second Saturday of Resurrection. Saturday is dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary.
term: A Syriac word meaning ‘offering’: the name the Syro-Malabar Church gives to the Holy Eucharist, the offering of Christ to the Father, made present on the altar, in which the faithful offer themselves with him. The Greek name Eucharist means ‘thanksgiving’. Both names together describe a Christian life: an offering made with thanks.

family.explain: On Easter evening Jesus came to his friends and said, ‘Peace be with you.’ They were scared and thought he was a ghost! Jesus said, ‘Look at my hands and feet. Touch me! A ghost doesn't have a body like me.’ Then he ate some fish in front of them. Jesus really rose from the dead, with his real body!
family.intention: We pray for families, that they may pray and sing together every day.
family.ask: Ask: “What hymn shall we sing together at our prayer tonight?”

illus: A Malayali family working in Kuwait found that their children were losing the habit of prayer: school, homework and screens filled every evening. The father decided to keep one rule. At half past seven the lamp was lit, the television switched off, and the family sat down for evening prayer, with the grandparents in Kerala joining by video call. Some evenings it was only ten minutes: a decade of the rosary, a short Gospel reading and one hymn the grandmother loved. Years later the eldest daughter, at university in Canada, wrote home: ‘At half past seven I still light a candle. When I sing that hymn I can hear Ammachi's voice, and I know I am not alone.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen in your true body, stand among us now and say to us: Peace be with you. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Above all, clothe yourselves with love (Colossians 3:14). Which virtue is falling off me for lack of love?
Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts (Colossians 3:15). Where do I need to let his peace make the call?
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly (Colossians 3:16). Does God's word have a room in my house?
Touch me and see (Luke 24:39). How does my faith in the bodily Resurrection change how I treat my body and others?
pm.resp: Lord, let your peace rule in our hearts.
interc: For Christian families, that they may be little churches of prayer, Scripture and song.
For families scattered by migration, that faith may keep them united.
For those who doubt the Resurrection, that the Risen Lord may stand among them.
For our beloved dead, that they may rise in glory on the last day.
For choirs and all who lead the singing in our parishes.
pm.close: Father, your Son rose in his true body and showed his wounds to his disciples. Make us thankful in all things, let the word of Christ dwell in our homes, and bring us with all your saints to the resurrection of the body. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells the Colossians: Above all, clothe yourselves with love, which binds everything together in perfect harmony. Love is the belt that holds all the other virtues in place.
He gives three gifts for a Christian home: let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts; let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; and sing psalms, hymns and spiritual songs to God with gratitude.

When a Kerala family lights the lamp at dusk and gathers to pray, read the Gospel and sing, that is Colossians 3 lived out. And Paul adds: whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks. Our whole life can become a Qurbana, an offering with thanks.

In the Gospel the Risen Lord stands among his disciples and says, Peace be with you. They think he is a ghost. He says: Look at my hands and my feet; touch me and see; a ghost does not have flesh and bones. And he eats a piece of fish before them.
Our faith is not in a ghost or an idea. Jesus is risen in his own body, glorified, still bearing his wounds. And the same Lord gives us his true Body and Blood at the altar.
Tonight, let us light the lamp, pray and sing together at home, and let his peace rule in our hearts. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus came back to his friends after he rose, they thought he was a ghost! But he said, ‘Touch me! Look at my hands!’ And he ate some fish. Jesus is really alive!
Tonight at family prayer, sing a happy hymn to Jesus, because he is risen.

concl: The Risen Lord is no ghost: he lives in his glorified body and gives himself to us as food.
Let love clothe us, his peace rule us, and his word dwell in our homes.
2027-04-10.resolve: This week, keep family evening prayer daily with the Gospel and a hymn, let Christ's peace decide, and do everything in his name with thanks.
